summary:
I've been working on a handful of related things across the site and the local AI stack.

The biggest chunk of work went into BudgetTracker's database layer. I rewrote all 22 repositories and 14 services from MSSQL to Postgres using Drizzle ORM — that's everything: schema, migrations, tenant-isolation SQL, the `AccessibleAccounts` CTE, money arithmetic, triggers for audit immutability and family constraints. Validated the whole thing against a real postgres:16 container (11/11 integration tests green). The migration script for copying the live data is built and verified; the last step is Ben creating the Supabase project and running the cutover, which needs credentials only he can supply.

On phillipsben.com I built the project hero image pipeline. Each project page gets a generated SDXL illustration, color-mapped into the site's two-tone palette, baked into a webp at build time. The process runs on a local Tesla P100 via ComfyUI: generate with a prompt from a per-slug dictionary, apply a duotone pass (ink or accent depending on whether the project is featured), output at about 100–180 KB. Getting the prompts right took some iteration — literal nouns consistently cue the wrong output, so everything is abstracted to dot fields, ripple patterns, and hub-and-spoke arrangements. I generated heroes for 11 projects in two batches and wired up a prebuild guard that fails the build if a featured project is missing one.

"Talk to Virtual Me" also shipped — a bounded career assistant on phillipsben.com that answers questions about my work using only what's published on the site. The backend routes across a local Gemma model via Switchboard and falls back to Claude Haiku when the GPU is busy. It passed 16/16 adversarial test cases before I called it done.

A few smaller things: I set up a store-arrival briefing that fires when I enter a geofence — it pulls the relevant TickTick shopping items, formats a voice note via Kokoro TTS, and sends both text and audio to Telegram before I'm through the door. A separate lightweight web page at list.phillipsben.com lets my wife add items to the same list without needing an account. The morning briefing runs the same way: weather, calendar from two Outlook ICS feeds, TickTick tasks, and a short Japanese hiragana practice segment, all assembled and delivered as a voice note at 6:30am.

highlights.oneLiner: Migrating all 22 repos and 14 services from MSSQL to Postgres/Drizzle ORM; data copy script built, blocked on Supabase credentials
Built SDXL hero image pipeline with duotone palette mapping; generated heroes for 11 projects via ComfyUI on the P100
Shipped bounded career assistant with GPU/Haiku fallback; 16/16 adversarial test cases passed
Store-arrival geofence briefing live; wife item-input page at list.phillipsben.com wired to same TickTick pipeline
